akapulko.about: Akapulko (Senna alata) is a medicinal plant traditionally used for common fungal skin infections. Its leaves are commonly prepared for external application to affected areas and are associated with traditional care for conditions such as ringworm and athlete's foot, particularly when itching and other skin irritation are present.
preparation_methods: Crush fresh leaves and apply directly to affected skin.
Prepare leaf extract for topical use.

alagao.about: Alagao (Premna odorata) is a traditional medicinal plant commonly associated with respiratory and digestive-related herbal preparations. It has been used traditionally for concerns such as cough, fever, and respiratory discomfort, with its leaves commonly prepared as a tea or decoction.
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink as herbal tea.
Use leaf decoction as a gargle.

aloe-vera.about: Aloe vera is a well-known medicinal plant valued for the soothing and moisturizing qualities of its leaf gel. The fresh gel is traditionally applied to the skin to help soothe irritation, moisturize dry areas, and support the care of minor wounds and burns.
preparation_methods: Apply fresh gel directly to skin.
Use gel as a topical treatment for minor burns.

ampalaya.about: Ampalaya (Momordica charantia) is a commonly used medicinal and food plant traditionally associated with blood sugar management and digestive support. Its leaves and fruits are also valued as a source of antioxidants and are commonly incorporated into food or prepared as a herbal tea.
preparation_methods: Cook leaves or fruits as vegetables.
Prepare leaf tea by boiling leaves in water.

Aratiles.about: Aratiles (Muntingia calabura), also known as Jamaican cherry or Panama berry, is a small fruit-bearing tree traditionally used in folk medicine for pain relief and respiratory concerns. Its leaves and flowers are commonly prepared as a decoction and are traditionally associated with relieving headaches, colds, and mild inflammation, while the ripe fruit is eaten fresh as a source of nutrients.
benefits: Helps relieve headaches and mild pain
Supports relief from colds and cough
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and flowers and drink as herbal tea.

atis.about: Atis (Annona squamosa) is a fruit-bearing plant with traditional medicinal uses involving digestive and skin-related concerns. Its leaves have been used in herbal preparations for digestive discomfort, while crushed leaves have also been traditionally applied externally for minor skin concerns.
benefits: Traditionally used for minor skin issues
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink as herbal tea.

banaba.about: Banaba (Lagerstroemia speciosa) is a widely recognized medicinal plant traditionally used in herbal preparations for blood sugar and urinary concerns. Its leaves are commonly prepared as tea or a decoction and are also associated with traditional support for urinary health and fluid balance.
preparation_methods: Boil fresh leaves and drink the decoction.

basil.about: Basil (Ocimum basilicum) is an aromatic herb commonly used in food and traditional herbal preparations. Its leaves are traditionally used to support digestion and general wellness, while its pleasant aroma is also associated with calming and relaxing effects.

bayabas.about: Bayabas (Psidium guajava) is a widely used medicinal and food plant known for its traditional applications in wound care and digestive concerns. Its leaves are commonly boiled and used as a wash for minor wounds or prepared as a decoction, and the plant is traditionally associated with antibacterial properties.
preparation_methods: Use boiled leaves as wound wash.

bignay.about: Bignay (Antidesma bunius) is a fruit-bearing plant with traditional uses related to digestive and urinary health. Its ripe fruit is also a source of antioxidants, while the leaves may be prepared as a traditional decoction for herbal use.
benefits: Rich in antioxidants from ripe fruit

calamansi.about: Calamansi (Citrus microcarpa) is a small citrus fruit valued for its vitamin C content and common use in traditional home remedies. It is often prepared as a diluted drink and is traditionally associated with support for coughs, colds, and general immune health.
preparation_methods: Use as a beverage for vitamin supplementation.

cassava.about: Cassava (Manihot esculenta) is an important root crop that has both nutritional and traditional medicinal uses. Its roots provide carbohydrates and an energy source, while the leaves have also been used traditionally after proper preparation. Thorough cooking and proper preparation are important before consumption.

dayap.about: Dayap (Citrus aurantiifolia) is a citrus plant traditionally used in preparations associated with respiratory and digestive support. Its juice provides vitamin C and may be consumed diluted or incorporated into traditional herbal preparations for concerns such as cough and digestive discomfort.

gumamela.about: Gumamela (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis) is a flowering plant that has long been used in traditional herbal practices. Its leaves and flowers are traditionally prepared for concerns such as fever, cough, and inflammation, including use as a tea or as a crushed-leaf external preparation.
preparation_methods: Boil flowers and leaves for tea.

ipil-ipil.about: Ipil-ipil (Leucaena leucocephala) is a multipurpose plant with several traditional uses, including applications related to wounds and digestive concerns. Its leaves have been prepared as a decoction or crushed for external use, and the plant has also been traditionally associated with antiparasitic applications.

kamantigi.about: Kamantigi (Impatiens balsamina) is a flowering plant traditionally used in folk medicine for skin-related concerns. Its leaves may be crushed or prepared as an extract for external use and are traditionally associated with soothing irritated skin, managing minor skin infections, and reducing inflammation.

kamias.about: Kamias (Averrhoa bilimbi) is a fruit-bearing plant traditionally used for several household herbal preparations. It has been associated with cough relief, support for healthy blood pressure, and certain skin concerns, with both fruit preparations and leaf decoctions used traditionally.

lagundi.about: Lagundi (Vitex negundo) is one of the most widely recognized Philippine medicinal plants traditionally used for respiratory concerns. Its leaves are commonly prepared as a tea or decoction and are associated with relief of coughs and colds, sore throat, and fever, as well as traditional support for respiratory conditions.
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink as tea.

madre-de-cacao.about: Madre de Cacao (Gliricidia sepium) is a plant traditionally used for external skin and wound care. Its leaves may be crushed and applied externally or prepared as a wash, and traditional use associates the plant with support for minor wounds and certain skin infections because of its reported antifungal properties.

malunggay.about: Malunggay (Moringa oleifera) is a highly nutritious plant widely valued for its vitamins, minerals, and antioxidant content. Its leaves are commonly eaten as a vegetable or prepared as tea, making the plant an important traditional food source that supports overall nutrition and may help address nutritional deficiencies.

manga.about: Manga (Mangifera indica) is a familiar fruit tree whose leaves, bark, and fruit have traditional uses. The leaves may be prepared as a decoction for traditional herbal use, while the fruit provides antioxidants and can contribute to a healthy diet; the plant is also traditionally associated with digestive support.
preparation_methods: Consume fruit as part of a healthy diet.

Mangosteen.about: Mangosteen (Garcinia mangostana) is a tropical fruit tree valued both for its edible fruit and for the traditional medicinal use of its rind (pericarp). The rind is traditionally prepared as a decoction and is associated with support for diarrhea and digestive discomfort, while it is also recognized as a rich source of antioxidant compounds believed to help ease inflammation.
benefits: Supports digestive health and helps relieve diarrhea
preparation_methods: Boil dried rind and drink as a decoction.
Consume fresh fruit as part of a healthy diet.

oregano.about: Oregano (Plectranthus amboinicus) is an aromatic medicinal herb commonly used in traditional home remedies for respiratory discomfort. Its leaves are traditionally prepared as an extract or chewed fresh and are associated with helping relieve cough, soothe sore throat, and support respiratory health.
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink the extract.

pandan.about: Pandan (Pandanus amaryllifolius) is an aromatic plant widely used in cooking and traditional herbal practices. Its leaves are commonly used to add fragrance and flavor to food and may also be prepared as tea, with traditional uses associated with relaxation and digestive support.
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink as herbal tea.
Use fresh leaves in food preparation.

pansit-pansitan.about: Pansit-pansitan (Peperomia pellucida) is a small herb traditionally used for concerns involving uric acid, gout, and joint discomfort. The fresh leaves may be consumed as food or prepared together with the stems as a decoction, and traditional use associates the plant with support for joint health and relief of gout and arthritis symptoms.
benefits: Helps relieve gout and arthritis symptoms
preparation_methods: Prepare a decoction from leaves and stems.

peanut.about: Peanut (Arachis hypogaea) is a nutritious legume valued for its protein, healthy fats, and antioxidant content. Although primarily recognized as a food plant, its nutritional value makes it useful for supporting overall dietary needs, and its seeds can be consumed roasted, boiled, or incorporated into various dishes.

pomelo.about: Pomelo (Citrus maxima) is a large citrus fruit that is a good source of vitamin C and is traditionally valued as part of a healthy diet. Its fruit may be eaten fresh or consumed as juice, with traditional uses associated with supporting immune health and digestion and helping provide vitamin C.
preparation_methods: Use the juice as a vitamin C-rich beverage.

saluyot.about: Saluyot (Corchorus olitorius) is a leafy vegetable that provides vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber. It is commonly cooked as a vegetable or added to soups and is traditionally valued for supporting digestive health and helping with concerns such as constipation.

sambong.about: Sambong (Blumea balsamifera) is a well-known Philippine medicinal plant traditionally used for urinary and kidney-related concerns. Its leaves are commonly prepared as a tea or decoction, and the plant is recognized in traditional use for its diuretic properties and support of urinary tract health.
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink as tea.
Prepare leaf decoction for herbal use.

sampaloc.about: Sampaloc (Tamarindus indica) is a fruit-bearing tree commonly used as both a food and traditional medicinal plant. Its ripe fruit pulp is valued for its flavor and antioxidant content and is traditionally used to support digestion and help relieve constipation, including through fruit-based beverages.

sampasampalukan.about: Sampasampalukan (Phyllanthus niruri) is a small medicinal plant traditionally associated with urinary and kidney-related concerns. The whole plant may be prepared as a decoction or used in other herbal preparations, with traditional uses including support for urinary tract health and concerns involving kidney stones.
benefits: Traditionally used to help with kidney stones
preparation_methods: Boil the entire plant and drink the decoction.
Use fresh plant material in herbal preparations.

siling-labuyo.about: Siling-labuyo (Capsicum frutescens) is a small, hot chili pepper valued as a food plant and for its traditional medicinal applications. It contains antioxidant compounds and has traditionally been used in preparations associated with pain relief and metabolism, while topical preparations should be used with proper guidance.
preparation_methods: Prepare topical liniments under proper guidance.

sweet-potato.about: Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a nutritious root crop that provides vitamins, fiber, and antioxidant compounds. Its roots are commonly boiled or steamed, while young leaves can be cooked as vegetables, making the plant useful for supporting nutrition and digestive health.
preparation_methods: Boil or steam roots before consumption.

takip-kohol.about: Takip-kohol (Centella asiatica) is a traditional medicinal herb commonly associated with wound care, memory, and circulation. Its fresh leaves may be consumed or prepared as tea, and traditional use associates the plant with supporting wound healing, healthy circulation, and memory and focus.

tawa-tawa.about: Tawa-tawa (Euphorbia hirta) is a plant traditionally used in Philippine herbal practices for fever and respiratory concerns. The whole plant may be prepared as a decoction, and it has also been used traditionally as supportive herbal medicine for symptoms associated with dengue; it should not be considered a substitute for professional medical care.
benefits: Traditionally used to help manage dengue-related symptoms
preparation_methods: Boil the entire plant and drink the decoction.
Use fresh plant material in herbal preparations.

tsaang-gubat.about: Tsaang-gubat (Ehretia microphylla) is a medicinal plant recognized for its traditional use in managing digestive and stomach-related discomfort. Its leaves are commonly boiled and prepared as tea or a decoction, with traditional applications including stomach ache, indigestion, and diarrhea.
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink as herbal tea.

tuba.about: Tuba (Jatropha curcas) is a plant with traditional external applications for certain skin conditions and minor wounds. Because the plant can contain toxic compounds, its use requires proper preparation and guidance, and traditional preparations are intended for external use rather than casual consumption.
preparation_methods: Use only under proper guidance due to potential toxicity.

turmeric.about: Turmeric (Curcuma longa) is a widely used plant and culinary spice known for its traditional anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Its rhizomes can be prepared as tea or used as a spice, and traditional use associates turmeric with support for joint comfort, inflammation, and general immune health.
preparation_methods: Use rhizomes as a culinary spice.

Uray.about: Uray (Amaranthus spinosus), also known as spiny amaranth, is a leafy plant used both as a food source and in traditional herbal preparations. Its leaves are commonly cooked as a vegetable or boiled for tea, with traditional use associating the plant with diuretic effects, relief of fever, and support for healthy digestion.
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink as herbal tea.

yerba-buena.about: Yerba-buena (Mentha cordifolia) is an aromatic medicinal herb commonly used in traditional remedies for headaches, stomach aches, and minor pain. Its leaves may be prepared as tea, chewed fresh, or crushed for external use, making it a familiar household herb for mild discomfort.
preparation_methods: Boil leaves and drink as tea.
Chew fresh leaves for mild discomfort.
